routes.label: Find the distance between adjacent midpoints

question:
The five small shaded squares inside this unit square are congruent and have disjoint interiors. The midpoint of each side of the middle square coincides with one of the vertices of the other four small squares as shown. The common side length is \(\dfrac{a-\sqrt{2}}{b},\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers. What is \(a+b?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2016_AMC_12A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The midpoint condition creates a right triangle whose legs are half the common side length. This relates the middle square to the gap between the corner squares.

[Figure 1](figures/2016_AMC_12A_Q09_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(s>0\) be the common side length. Let \(P,Q\) be the inward vertices of the top-left and top-right corner squares, and let \(V\) be the top vertex of the middle square.

The two top corner squares each extend a distance \(s\) inward from a vertical side and a distance \(s\) below the top side. Thus \(P,Q\) are at the same height, and
\[
PQ=1-2s.
\]
By the stated midpoint condition, \(P\) and \(Q\) are midpoints of the two sides of the middle square meeting at \(V\). Hence \(VP=VQ=\frac{s}{2}\), and \(\angle PVQ=90^\circ\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
PQ=\sqrt{\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2}
=\frac{s}{\sqrt2}.
\]
Equating the two expressions for this gap gives
\[
1-2s=\frac{s}{\sqrt2},
\qquad
s=\frac{\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2+1}.
\]
To obtain the requested form, multiply numerator and denominator by \(2\sqrt2-1\):
\[
s=\frac{\sqrt2(2\sqrt2-1)}{8-1}
=\frac{4-\sqrt2}{7}.
\]
This solution is positive and satisfies \(1-2s=\frac{s}{\sqrt2}>0\), as the gap requires. Therefore \(a=4\), \(b=7\), and \(\boxed{a+b=11}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
